I have been farming these 4.1 mu in Quzhou for 50 years, and at 76 I know what works on my land. My wife and I are the only two in the household now, so we have to manage the labor ourselves—we cannot take big risks or try fancy new methods. I will keep 2.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and plant 2.0 mu to cotton, the same split I have used for years. 

For the winter wheat, I will rotary-till the soil and sow improved seed in early October. I usually put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, then topdress with urea at green-up and jointing. With the well pump I can irrigate four times—winter irrigation, green-up, jointing, and filling—which is what my neighbors do and what has given me stable yields around 950 jin per mu.

The summer maize goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There is no time to plough; we no-till plant directly into the stubble. I always buy hybrid maize seed from the seed shop—saved seed does not yield well for maize. I apply one bag of compound fertilizer at planting and irrigate twice if the weather is dry, usually at the big-flare and filling stages. 

For cotton, I rotary-till in mid-April and sow improved cotton seed. Cotton needs a lot of pesticide attention—bollworm and aphids come every year—so I spray roughly 18 times across the season. I apply compound fertilizer as a base and irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll-setting. I expect about 500 jin per mu of seed cotton. 

I do not chase maximum yields anymore; I aim for steady, manageable output that my wife and I can handle without hiring help.
